heard: Tiny dwarf galaxies are leaking oxygen into deep space. Every breath we take was forged inside a star. When stars explode, a supernovae, they expel that oxygen. Most massive galaxies have enough gravity to trap it, but NASA's Hubble found these tiny systems have lost nearly all their oxygen. Violent galactic winds act like a massive cosmic purge. These gales blast oxygen entirely out of the galaxy's reach. These tiny systems are the universe's most efficient chemical polluters. That's why tiny dwarf galaxies are leaking oxygen into deep space.
